Assigning ASVs with DADA2

Roger Calvas

2026-10-14

Setear variables de ambientes

Semilla y threads

# Set the seed for reproducibility
set.seed(9473)

# Let's make a parameter to set the number of threads 
n_threads = 20

Tiempo de inicio

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Load Packages

# install.packages("janitor")
# Efficient package loading with pacman 
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, dada2, 
               patchwork, DT, phyloseq, janitor, install = FALSE)

Objetivos del archivo:

  1. Inferir el modelo de error de DADA2 tanto en las R1 como R2
  2. Asignar ASVs usando el modelo de error tanto en R1 como R2
  3. Empalmar las secuencias para generar una tabla de ASVs continua
  4. Crear el primer draft de la tabla de recuento de ASVs
  5. Chequear estadistica de ASVs
  6. Quitar quimeras
  7. Asignar taxonomia con UNITE
  8. Guardar los archivos relevantes: asv_table, asvs_fasta, tax_table, y sample_data
  9. Crear S4 R data object, en este caso llamado phyloseq, desde la tabla asv_table, tax_table, y metadata.Unificando todo en un solo objeto de datos.

Input

  1. Fastq filtrados de 01_QC_DADA2.Rmd
  2. Vector de sample_names
  3. Metadata

Output

  1. Tabla de conteo de asvs: asv_table (Con y sin nombre de secuencia)
  2. Tabla de taxonomia asignada tax_table
  3. Un objeto phyloseq raw (S4 object): raw_physeq.RData

Cargar datos

Cargar fastqs

# Place filtered seq files into a variable 
filtered_fastqs_path <- "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs"

# Intuition check:
filtered_fastqs_path
## [1] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs"
# Create Forward vector 
filtered_forward_reads <- 
  list.files(filtered_fastqs_path, pattern = "R1_filtered.fastq.gz",
             full.names = TRUE)
# Check 
filtered_forward_reads[1:5]
## [1] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-004_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [2] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-006_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [3] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-007_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"

## [5] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-018_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
# Reverse vector 
filtered_reverse_reads <- 
    list.files(filtered_fastqs_path, pattern = "R2_filtered.fastq.gz",
             full.names = TRUE)

# Check 
filtered_reverse_reads[1:5]
## [1] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-004_R2_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [2] "data/16s/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-006_R2_filtered.fastq.gz"

Nombres de muestras

# Create vector of sample names from the filenames
sample_names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(filtered_forward_reads), "_"), `[`, 1) 

# Intuition Check 
head(sample_names)
## [1] "ANF-004" "ANF-006" "ANF-007" "ANF-011" "ANF-018" "ANF-021"

Prediccion de errores

Funcion de estimacion para bins

# Declarar los bins del secuenciador
binnedQs <- c(2, 11, 25, 37)

# Crear la funcion en base a los bins
binnedErrFun <- makeBinnedQualErrfun(binnedQs)

Calcular los errores

# Forward Reads con binned err fun
error_forward_reads <- 
  learnErrors(filtered_forward_reads, multithread = n_threads, nbases = 3e8, errorEstimationFunction = binnedErrFun, verbose = TRUE)
## 303160127 total bases in 1328492 reads from 21 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
## Initializing error rates to maximum possible estimate.
## selfConsist step 1 .....................
##    selfConsist step 2
##    selfConsist step 3
##    selfConsist step 4
##    selfConsist step 5
##    selfConsist step 6
## Convergence after  6  rounds.
# Forward Error Plot 
forward_error_plot <- 
  plotErrors(error_forward_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) + 
  labs(title = "Forward Reads: Error Model")

# Reverse Reads con binned err fun
error_reverse_reads <- 
  learnErrors(filtered_reverse_reads, multithread = n_threads, nbases = 3e8, errorEstimationFunction = binnedErrFun, verbose = TRUE)
## 311213814 total bases in 1401413 reads from 22 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
## Initializing error rates to maximum possible estimate.
## selfConsist step 1 ......................
##    selfConsist step 2
##    selfConsist step 3
##    selfConsist step 4
##    selfConsist step 5
##    selfConsist step 6
##    selfConsist step 7
## Convergence after  7  rounds.
# Reverse Error Plot 
reverse_error_plot <- 
  plotErrors(error_reverse_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) + 
  labs(title = "Reverse Reads: Error Model")

# Look at the plots together 
forward_error_plot + reverse_error_plot

Preguntas 1: La secuencia tenia calidades binned y como se ajusto la curva de error?

[La secuencia tenia bins en: ‘2, 11, 25, 37’ y la curva de error se ajusto mejor al aplicar el modelo para secuenciadores de bins]

Inferir e inspeccionar ASVs

Inferir ASVs

# Infer ASVs on the forward sequences
dada_forward <- 
  dada(filtered_forward_reads, 
       err = error_forward_reads,
       multithread = n_threads)

Figura de los largos de los ASVs

# Inspect the distribution of sequence lengths of all ASVs in data set 
plot_ASVLength_raw <- 
  data.frame(Seq_Length = nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Seq_Length )) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  # include the x-axis scales
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, maxLength_ASV + 5)) + 
  labs(y = "Number of ASVs", x = "Raw ASV Length (bps)")

# Show the plot
plot_ASVLength_raw
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_bar()`).

Preguntas 2: Cual es el largo esperado de los ASVs sin primers? Cual fue la region minima de solapamiento? Cual es el valor default de region minima de solapamiento? [En ITS es variable entonces queremos ver una curva con forma de campana, sobre todo que tenga un decrecimiento suavizado. La region minima de solapamiento fue 12 porque ese es el valor default de la funcion]

Trim ASV length

# Subset only ASVs that are 245 bps long
# Filtrar para secuencias entre 400 y 440 pares de bases
raw_ASV_table_trimmed <- raw_ASV_table[, nchar(colnames(raw_ASV_table)) >= 403 & nchar(colnames(raw_ASV_table)) <= 440]

Remover Chimeras

# Remove the chimeras in the raw ASV table
noChimeras_ASV_table <- 
  removeBimeraDenovo(raw_ASV_table_trimmed, 
                     method="consensus", 
                     multithread = n_threads, 
                     verbose=TRUE)
## Identified 13578 bimeras out of 14583 input sequences.
# Check the dimensions
dim(noChimeras_ASV_table)
## [1]   34 1005
# Chimera removal compared to raw  
percRetained_chimerasRaw <-sum(noChimeras_ASV_table)/sum(raw_ASV_table)
percRetained_chimerasRaw
## [1] 0.7869002
# Plot it 
plot_ASVLength_NoChimeras <- 
  data.frame(Seq_Length_NoChim = nchar(getSequences(noChimeras_ASV_table))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Seq_Length_NoChim )) + 
  geom_histogram()+ 
  # include the x-axis scales
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, maxLength_ASV + 5)) + 
  labs(y = "Number of ASVs \n (Post-Chimera Removal)", 
       x = "ASV Length (bps)")

# Show the plot
plot_ASVLength_NoChimeras

Track the read counts

# A little function to identify number seqs 
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))

# Make the table to track the seqs 
track <- cbind(sapply(dada_forward, getN),
               sapply(dada_reverse, getN),
               sapply(merged_ASVs, getN),
               rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table))

# Update column names to be more informative (most are missing at the moment!)
colnames(track) <- c("denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")
rownames(track) <- row.names(noChimeras_ASV_table)

# Generate a dataframe to track the reads through our DADA2 pipeline
track_counts_df <- 
  track %>%
  # make it a dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_names")

# Now let's add a column for the number of ASVs
# First, intuition check that the samples match 
stopifnot(track_counts_df$sample_names == row.names(noChimeras_ASV_table))

# Now, let's add a new column with the number of ASVs
track_counts_df <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  mutate(num_ASVs = rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table > 1))

# Visualize it in table format 
DT::datatable(track_counts_df)
# Plot it!
track_counts_df %>%
  pivot_longer(denoisedF:nochim, names_to = "read_type", values_to = "num_reads") %>%
  mutate(read_type = fct_relevel(read_type, "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = read_type, y = num_reads, fill = read_type)) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = sample_names), color = "grey") + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") + 
  labs(x = "Filtering Step", y = "Number of Sequences") + 
  theme_bw()

Profundidad, riqueza y ASVs por profundidad

# Cual es la profundidad por muestra
plot_ReadDepth <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = nochim)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  labs(x = "Total # of Sequences", y = "# of Samples") + 
  theme_bw()
plot_ReadDepth
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

# What is the ASV richness per sample? 
plot_ASVRichness <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num_ASVs)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  labs(x = "Total # of ASVs", y = "# of Samples") + 
  theme_bw()
plot_ASVRichness
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

# Now, let's look at the relationship of ASVs and Sequencing depth 
plot_ReadDepth_ASVRichness <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = nochim, y = num_ASVs)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  labs(x = "Total # of Sequences", y = "# of ASVs") + 
  theme_bw()
plot_ReadDepth_ASVRichness

# Show the plots together 
plot_ReadDepth + plot_ASVRichness + plot_ReadDepth_ASVRichness + 
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')

# How many ASVs? 
num_ASVs <- dim(final_ASV_table_withSeqs)[1] # select the number of rows
num_ASVs 
## [1] 1005
# which is where we will place the new operational ASV names 
ASV_headers <- vector(num_ASVs, mode = "character")

# Let's mae sure we have an empty vector!
ASV_headers[1:5]
## [1] "" "" "" "" ""
length(ASV_headers) # looks good! 
## [1] 1005
# Ahora creemos un vector con ASVs numerados usando un loop
for (i in 1:num_ASVs) {
  # Add leading zero to ASV name so they print in correct order.
  ASV_number <- sprintf("%04d", i)
  # Now, rename each spot in the ASV header vector as we loop through the for loop
  ASV_headers[i] <- paste(">ASV", ASV_number, sep = "_")
}

# Intuition check
ASV_headers[1:5]

##### Prepare tax table 
# 1. Add the ASV sequences from the rownames to a column 
new_tax_table <- 
  taxa_train%>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "ASVseqs")

ASV_tax_table <- 
  new_tax_table %>%
  # add rownames from count table for phyloseq handoff
  mutate(ASV = rownames(final_ASV_table)) %>%
  # Reorder the columns
  dplyr::select(Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species, ASV, ASVseqs)

rownames(ASV_tax_table) <- ASV_tax_table$ASV

3. Creacion de objeto phyloseq

Importar metadata y agregar las calidades de agua a las muestras

# Importar la tabla de promedios de calidad de agua
agua_df <- read_csv("data/16s/metadata/agua_promedios.csv", col_names = TRUE) %>%
  clean_names()
## Rows: 5 Columns: 9
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (1): Localidad
## dbl (8): avg_tds_ppm, avg_temp_c, avg_ph, avg_conductivity, avg_nitrates_mg_...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
# Estandarizar los nombres de las muestras
track_counts_df$sample_names <- sapply(strsplit(track_counts_df$sample_names, "_"), '[', 1)
  
# Como se ve despues? 
head(track_counts_df)
##   sample_names denoisedF denoisedR merged nochim num_ASVs
## 1      ANF-004     59712     59758  59339  56878        7
## 2      ANF-006     72647     72653  70814  66238       30
## 3      ANF-007     58554     58553  58002  49883       22
## 4      ANF-011     68187     68427  65581  47117       65
## 5      ANF-018     67407     67529  61224  38379      149
## 6      ANF-021     58906     58939  57170  45946       71
# Ensamblar la metadata  
metadata_fixed <-read_csv("data/16s/metadata/metadata.csv", col_names = TRUE) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # Renombrar la columna de nombres para que sea sample_names
  dplyr::rename(sample_names = codigo) %>%
  
  # Elimina las filas que no tenian muestras secuenciadas
  drop_na(sample_names) %>%
  
  # Eliminar filas que tengan guiones bajos pero no codigo de muestra
  filter(!str_detect(sample_names, "^_+$|^-+$")) %>%
  
  # Estandarizar el nombre de las muestras
  mutate(sample_names = str_replace_all(sample_names, " ", "-")) %>%
  mutate(sample_names = str_trim(sample_names)) %>%
  # Inyectar las calidades promedio de agua por localidad
  left_join(agua_df, by = "localidad") %>%
  
  # Inner_join para ignorar las cosas no secuenciadas y añadir stats DADA2
  inner_join(track_counts_df, by = "sample_names") %>%
  
  # Prueba de sanidad para que solo haya un registro por muestra
  distinct(sample_names, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  
  # Phyloseq exige que los identificadores de muestra estén asignados como 'rownames' 
  # para poder ensamblar el objeto S4. Sin embargo, las herramientas de Tidyverse 
  # (como dplyr y ggplot2) operan sobre columnas explícitas y no leen los rownames.
  # Como la función 'column_to_rownames' consume (elimina) la columna que se le pasa, 
  # creamos una copia temporal para sacrificarla en este paso. Esto satisface el 
  # requisito de Phyloseq y conserva la columna original 'sample_names' intacta 
  # para uso futuro en tidyverse y facil acceso a la metadata
  mutate(rownames_temp = sample_names) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "rownames_temp")
## New names:
## Rows: 263 Columns: 76
## ── Column specification
## ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Delimiter: "," chr
## (34): codigo, Familia, Género, Especie, Afinidades taxonómicas (observa... dbl
## (37): Latitud (inicio), Longitud (inicio), Elevación (inicio), Latitud ... lgl
## (2): Cantón, ...39 time (3): Hora, Hora de inicio, Hora de fin
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data. ℹ
## Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
## • `` -> `...34`
## • `` -> `...35`
## • `` -> `...39`
# Verificar dimensiones finales
dim(metadata_fixed)
## [1] 34 89

Pasar a phyloseq

raw_physeq <-
  phyloseq::phyloseq(otu_table(final_ASV_table, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
         sample_data(metadata_fixed),
         tax_table(as.matrix(ASV_tax_table)))

raw_physeq

## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 1005 taxa and 34 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 34 samples by 89 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 1005 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
#View(as(sample_data(raw_physeq), "data.frame"))
#save
save(raw_physeq, file = "data/16s/02_Assign_ASVs/raw_physeq.RData")
